polityNote: Russian Empire (from March 1917 the Russian Republic): Little Russia, Sloboda Ukraine, New Russia, the right-bank (south-western) governorates and Bessarabia (Russian from 16/28 May 1812). Dates converted from Old Style. Gradonachalstvos with their own administration (Odessa, Nikolaev, Kerch-Enikale, Sevastopol) are drawn inside the governorate the 1897 census grouped them with. Wartime occupation (1915–17) not depicted.

sources.says: ПСЗ-1 № 20205 (6/29.03.1802): Bogucharsky, Ostrogozhsky, Starobelsky uyezds moved to Voronezh; 1803 division into 10 uyezds; next outer change 1824.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Воронежская губерния
sources.says: Voronezh received the three Sloboda uyezds in March 1802 and returned Starobelsk uyezd on 9 Jan 1824.

spans.dateNote: Report approved 1802-03-06 O.S., Senate decree published 1802-03-29 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 20205); approval date used (+12 → 1802-03-18). The 1803 re-division into 10 uyezds (ПСЗ-1 № 20660) was internal; the 1797–1802 composition (with Ostrogozhsk, Boguchar) is outside this span.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Харьковская (Слободско-Украинская) губерния
sources.says: ПСЗ-1 № 29729 (09.01.1824): Starobelsk uyezd joined from Voronezh to Sloboda-Ukrainian governorate.

sources.title: Старобельский уезд — Википедия (oldid 153208688)
sources.says: Starobelsk uyezd in Voronezh 1802–1824, returned to Sloboda governorate by decree of 9 January 1824.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Харьковская (Слободско-Украинская) губерния
sources.says: ПСЗ-2 № 8654 (5/20.12.1835): renamed Kharkov governorate; the only later entry (1861) moves villages between its own uyezds.

sources.title: Харьковская губерния — Википедия (oldid 153208694)
sources.says: Formed 1835 with 11 uyezds; Izyum and Starobelsk uyezds left only in 1920 for Donetsk governorate.

spans.dateNote: Rename only (same territory): 1835-12-05 O.S. (published 20.12) → 1835-12-17. No outer change 1835–1897 in Den; none 1897–1917 per the Wikipedia history (first change 1920).

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Екатеринославская губерния
sources.says: ПСЗ-1 № 20684 (27.03.1803): all land between the Berestovaya and the Orel joined to Poltava governorate from Ekaterinoslav.

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Черниговская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5335317), т. XXXVIIIa (1903), с. 590–599
sources.says: Chernigov’s southern border with Poltava and Kharkov was fixed in 1802 when Little Russia was split; unchanged since.

sources.title: Полтавская губерния — Википедия (oldid 155028573)
sources.says: 15 uyezds by 1803; this division lasted until 1920, when uyezds went to Kremenchug governorate.

spans.dateNote: Senate decree 1803-03-27 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 20684) → 1803-04-08. The 1803 creation of Zenkov, Kobelyaki, Lokhvitsa uyezds was internal. Den’s Kharkov and Ekaterinoslav lists show no later change on Poltava’s eastern/southern lines.

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Черниговская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5335317), т. XXXVIIIa (1903), с. 590–599
sources.says: Area excludes parcels ceded to Kiev and Mogilev governorates by Committee of Ministers decisions of 1889 and 1894; northern/eastern borders unchanged since 17th c.

spans.dateNote: Conservative start, not a change date: ESBE gives only the years (1889, 1894) of the last outer-line transfers; one search hit (unverified) dates a Novozybkov→Gomel parcel to 1894-02-18. 1 Jan 1895 is the first day certainly after both. No change 1895–1917 known (first change: four northern uyezds to Gomel governorate 1919).

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Черниговская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5335317), т. XXXVIIIa (1903), с. 590–599
sources.says: Parcels of Chernigov governorate passed to Kiev (and Mogilev) governorate by Committee of Ministers decisions of 1889 and 1894.

sources.title: Киевская губерния — Википедия (oldid 152619897)
sources.says: 12 uyezds at the end of the 19th century; Berdichev entered the governorate in the 1840s and became an uyezd seat.

spans.dateNote: Conservative start after the 1889/1894 Chernigov parcels (day unknown). Earlier outer change: Berdichev from Volhynia 1844. No change 1895–1917 found.

sources.title: История Бердичева — Википедия (oldid 154747025)
sources.says: In 1844 the town of Berdichev was cut off to Makhnovka uyezd of Kiev governorate; December 1845 made a town and uyezd seat.

sources.title: «Административный статус Бердичева» (berdychiv.in.ua)
sources.says: Senate decree of 21 Feb 1844 moved Berdichev from Zhitomir uyezd of Volhynia to Makhnovka uyezd of Kiev governorate.

sources.title: «Адміністративно-територіальний поділ Заславщини наприкінці XVIII – початку XX ст.» (perspekt.org.ua)
sources.says: Volhynia and Podolia uyezds consolidated 1797–1803; final establishment (штат) of both governorates issued 19 July 1804; Volhynia 12 uyezds.

spans.dateNote: Senate decree 1844-02-21 O.S. → 1844-03-04 (the day is from a local-history page; the year is confirmed by Wikipedia). No later outer change found to 1917 (the 1912 Kholm governorate was cut from Lublin and Siedlce only).

sources.title: О. Є. Маркова, «Подільська губернія», Енциклопедія історії України, дод. т. 1 (2021)
sources.says: Borders of the governorate and its division into 12 uyezds were finally settled in 1804; neighbours Volhynia, Kiev, Kherson, Bessarabia, Austrian Galicia.

sources.title: «Адміністративно-територіальний поділ Заславщини наприкінці XVIII – початку XX ст.» (perspekt.org.ua)
sources.says: Final establishment (штат) of the Volhynia and Podolia governorates issued 19 July 1804 after the 1797–1803 consolidation.

spans.dateNote: Штат of 1804-07-19 O.S. → 1804-07-31. Kherson side: Den’s Kherson list shows no change after 1802. No later change found to 1917.

sources.title: Southern Bessarabia — Wikipedia (oldid 1371865043)
sources.says: Transfer took place in October 1878: from 13 to 18 October Russia took over Southern Bessarabia as Romanian officials withdrew (Kellogg 1995).

sources.title: Измаильский уезд — Википедия (oldid 155147299)
sources.says: In 1878 the territory ceded in 1856 was returned to Russia and formed Izmail uyezd.

spans.dateNote: Treaty of Berlin 1878-07-13 N.S.; actual takeover 13–18 Oct 1878 (calendar of the source not stated; October in either). Month precision. Izmail uyezd’s borders were reworked in 1904 but only against Akkerman/Bender (internal). Oblast renamed governorate 1873-10-28 O.S. (= 11-09).

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Херсонская (Николаевская) губерния
sources.says: ПСЗ-1 № 20449 (08.10.1802): Nikolaev governorate formed from Novorossiya with Elisavetgrad, Olviopol, Tiraspol, Kherson uyezds; 1803 renamed Kherson.

spans.dateNote: Decree 1802-10-08 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 20449) → 1802-10-20. Den lists no later change of the outer line. In 1804 Taurida and Kherson negotiated the demarcation of the Dnieper/Konka floodplain (Kravchuk 2014) without a decree in ПСЗ; treated as demarcation of the 1802 line.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Херсонская (Николаевская) губерния
sources.says: ПСЗ-1 № 20760 (15.05.1803): seat moved to Kherson, renamed Kherson governorate; later entries (1806, 1825, 1828, 1834) only re-cut its own uyezds.

spans.dateNote: Rename 1803-05-15 O.S. → 1803-05-27. Odessa and Nikolaev gradonachalstvos (separate administrations) lie inside the 1897 Odessa/Kherson uyezd atoms and are drawn within the governorate, as the 1897 census counted them.

sources.title: «Генерал А. П. Ермолов и Черноморское казачье войско…» (roskav.ru)
sources.says: Decree of 11 April 1820 subordinated the Black Sea Host to the Georgian Corps; its lands left Taurida for Caucasus governorate administration.

sources.title: Таврическая губерния — Википедия (oldid 153227734)
sources.says: In 1820 Tmutarakan uyezd passed to the Black Sea Host oblast; Yalta uyezd formed 1838, Berdyansk 1843.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Таврическая губерния
sources.says: After 1802 only internal entries: Kerch-Enikale gradonachalstvo 1821, Yalta 1838, Berdyansk 1842, Sevastopol gradonachalstvo 1873.

spans.dateNote: 1820-04-11 O.S. → 1820-04-23. Kerch-Enikale (1821) and Sevastopol (1873) gradonachalstvos had their own administration but are separate 1897 atoms grouped under Taurida by the census; drawn inside Taurida. No change 1897–1917.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Екатеринославская губерния
sources.says: ПСЗ-3 № 4466 (19.05.1887): Taganrog gradonachalstvo and Rostov uyezd joined to the Don Host oblast; ПСЗ-3 № 4701 deferred execution to 01.01.1888.

sources.title: РНБ, «Справочные материалы об изменениях внутренних и внешних границ губерний Европейской России (1775–1897)» (по В. Э. Дену, 1902) — Область Войска Донского
sources.says: Same 1887 law re-cut Rostov and Taganrog okrugs from the gradonachalstvo, Rostov uyezd, Miussky okrug and part of Cherkassk okrug.

spans.dateNote: Effective 1888-01-01 O.S. (ПСЗ-3 № 4701) → 1888-01-13. No later outer change to 1917 (the 1872/1874 Aleksandrovsk–Mariupol re-cut is internal and earlier).
